Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (Scch-17) Dated This The 18Th Day Of January 2020 Present: Shri Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., Ll.B., Xix Addl. Judge & Member, Mact. Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.5820/2017, 5821/2017 & 5822/2017 Petitioner in Mvc Shri Yukthasri S.J., 5820/2017 Daughter of Janardhan S.L., Aged about 9 years, Residing at No.95, Shivakote Village, Near Lakshmi, Narasimhaswamy Temple, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk Bengaluru -560 089. Petitioner being minor represented by his father Janardhana S.L. the natural guardian. (By Pleader Shri H.R. Jayaram) Petitioner in Mvc Smt.Shwetha, 5821/2017 Wife of Janardhan S.L., Aged about 33 years, Residing at No.95, Shivakote Village, Near Lakshmi, Narasimhaswamy Temple, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru-560 089. 2 Scch-17 Mvc 5820/2017 to 5822/2017 (By Pleader Shri H.R. texts.facts: The petitioners have filed these respective claim petitions in MVC 5820/2017 to 5822/2017 against the respondents U/s 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-, Rs.10,00,000/- and Rs.75,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioners in a road traffic accident. 2. All these petitions are arising out of the same accident, hence, these petitions are clubbed and taken together for common discussion. In Mvc Shri Yukthasri S.J vs In All 1Shriram General Insurance Co. ... on 18 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118706443/ 2 3. The brief contents of all the petitions are as under: The allegation of the petitioners is that, on 28.4.2017 at about 3.00 p.m. the petitioners in MVC 5820/2017 & 5821/2017 were the occupants of the car bearing No.KA-50-N- 6867, which was driven by the petitioner in MVC 5822/2017 from Tumkur towards Gubbi slowly cautiously by observing all the traffic norms , when they reached infront of Boralingeswara Condiment, Heggere, at that time a lorry bearing No.KA-51-5486 came from opposite direction with 4 SCCH-17 MVC 5820/2017 to 5822/2017 high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others dashed against the car. Due to the impact, the petitioners sustained grievous injuries. Immediately they were shifted to Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur, wherein they took the first aid treatment, and then they were shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient. 4. The contention of the petitioner in MVC No.5820/2017 is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 9 years, student. Due to the accidental injuries, she could not able to lead normal life as she was doing prior to the accident. 5. The contention of the petitioner in MVC No.5821/2017 is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged In Mvc Shri Yukthasri S.J vs In All 1Shriram General Insurance Co. ... on 18 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118706443/ 3 about 33 years, Self employee, Textile & Readymade Garments and earning a sum of Rs.13,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, she could not do the work as earlier. 6. The contention of the petitioner in MVC No.5822/2017 is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged 5 SCCH-17 MVC 5820/2017 to 5822/2017 about 39 years, doing business of Textile and Readymade Garments at SLN Collection, Hesaraghatta, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.45,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, he could not do the work as earlier. 7. The contention of the petitioners is that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing NO.KA-31-5486. So, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners. Contending the above facts, the petitioners have filed these respective claim petitions and prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 8. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed the written statement. 9. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 in all the cases are as under: The contention of the respondent is that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-31-5486 and its validity. In Mvc Shri Yukthasri S.J vs In All 1Shriram General Insurance Co. ... on 18 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118706443/ 4 6 SCCH-17 MVC 5820/2017 to 5822/2017 Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S.134 and S.158(6) of the MV Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-50-N-6867 and not on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing NO.KA-31-5486. Further contended that the accident took place on 28.4.2017 and the complaint was lodged on 2.5.2017, after a lapse of 4 days from the date of alleged accident and no valid reasons assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint. Further contended that the lorry bearing NO.KA-31-54867 was not having valid permit to ply. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioners as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss all the claim petitions with cost. 10. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 in all the cases are as under: The contention of the respondent is that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on 7 SCCH-17 MVC 5820/2017 to 5822/2017 facts. 20. On perusal of evidence available on records, it reveals that, to prove their case, the father of the petitioner in MVC 5820/2017 is examined as PW1 and petitioners in MVC 5821/2017 and 5822/2017 have examined themselves as PW2 and PW3 and they have stated in their evidence by reiterating 12 SCCH-17 MVC 5820/2017 to 5822/2017 the contents of petition. 21. To prove the involvement of the alleged lorry and to In Mvc Shri Yukthasri S.J vs In All 1Shriram General Insurance Co. ... on 18 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118706443/ 9 prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the alleged lorry, in support of oral evidence, the petitioners have relied upon the copy of police investigation papers and the same are marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P4 and Ex.P20 i.e. copy of FIR, mahazar, wound certificate, charge sheet, Complaint. On perusal of Ex-P1, Ex.P20 and Ex.P4 i.e. copy of FIR, complaint and charge sheet, it reveals that, Tumkur Rural police have registered a case as against the driver of the alleged lorry bearing registration No.ka-31-5486 in Cr.No.89/2017 and after completion of investigation, the investigating officer have filed the charge sheet as against the driver of the alleged lorry for the offences punishable U/s.279, 337 and 338 of IPC. 22.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents argued by reiterating the contents of written statement filed by them and also evidence put forth by RW1 and RW2. Further he argued that, the alleged accident has occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the car as he was driving the car in a rash and negligent manner. Further he argued that, the petitioners have failed to prove their case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost.
